Manufacturers weaponized this to prevent repair by embedding software locks in devices -- circumventing diagnostic software became a federal offense even when no copyright infringement was intended. The Library of Congress conducts triennial rulemakings to grant temporary exemptions. The October 28, 2024 final rule (9th triennial proceeding) significantly expanded repair exemptions to cover smartphones, tablets, laptops, appliances, motor vehicles, marine vessels, and agricultural machinery through October 2027. Separately, as of 2025-2026, over 30 US states have introduced right-to-repair bills, with laws in effect in California, Colorado, Minnesota, New York, and Oregon requiring manufacturers to provide parts, tools, and documentation. The core conflict: Section 1201's anti-circumvention regime allows manufacturers to use copyright law as a platform lock-in mechanism for physical goods.

pairs.source_text: What interoperability and data portability legislation emerged in 2025-2026?
pairs.source_norm: what interoperability and data portability legislation emerged in 2025-2026?
pairs.target_text: Utah's Digital Choice Act (HB 418, signed March 27, 2025 by Governor Spencer Cox, effective July 1, 2026) is the most aggressive US state data portability law. It requires social media companies to: provide users access to transfer and share personal data including their social graph (connections, content, interactions, metadata) across platforms; implement transparent third-party-accessible interoperability interfaces; and enable real-time data sharing when users migrate. Utah's 2026 amendment (HB 408) added requirements for real-time transfer, user-selectable data portions, and consent requirements for including others' interactions. At the EU level, the EU Data Act (in force January 11, 2024, substantive provisions applicable September 12, 2025) requires data processing service providers to facilitate customer switching through open standardized interfaces and data portability. By 2026, 15 US states have comprehensive data privacy laws with portability provisions. The EU's Interoperable Europe Act entered into force April 11, 2024, mandating interoperability assessments for EU public services.

pairs.source_text: What did the FCC's Carterfone decision (1968) rule and what did it allow?
pairs.source_norm: what did the fcc's carterfone decision (1968) rule and what did it allow?
pairs.target_text: On June 26, 1968, the FCC voted 6-0 in the Carterfone decision (13 F.C.C.2d 420) to overturn AT&T/Bell System tariff restrictions that banned 'foreign attachments' to the telephone network. Thomas Carter's device connected two-way mobile radios to phone lines for oil field workers. The FCC ruled AT&T's restrictions were 'unreasonable, unlawful, and unreasonably discriminatory under the Communications Act of 1934.' Bell System responded by requiring 'protective connecting arrangements' (PCAs) -- costly interface devices customers had to lease from AT&T -- effectively creating a compliance tax. The FCC eliminated PCA requirements in 1977 via Part 68 registration, replacing them with self-certification. This opened the market for third-party phones, modems, answering machines, fax machines, and eventually the equipment that enabled the internet.

pairs.source_text: What is the historical chain from anti-scrip to digital data portability?
pairs.source_norm: what is the historical chain from anti-scrip to digital data portability?
pairs.target_text: The legislative arc spans 140+ years with a consistent principle: when a platform controls a critical resource (wages, network access, data), law eventually mandates portability and interoperability. Anti-scrip laws (1880s-1938) banned captive payment ecosystems. Carterfone (1968) banned captive equipment ecosystems. The AT&T MFJ (1984) structurally broke a vertically integrated network monopolist. DMCA 1201 (1998) inadvertently created new lock-in via copyright, now being rolled back through triennial exemptions and state right-to-repair laws. The EU DMA (2024 compliance) and DOJ v. Google (2025 remedies) attack digital platform lock-in through regulation and antitrust respectively. Utah's Digital Choice Act (2026) mandates real-time social graph interoperability. Each generation of law addresses the same market failure -- monopoly control over switching costs -- in the dominant infrastructure medium of its era: company towns, telephone networks, digital platforms.

pairs.source_text: Counter-claim: Data sovereignty — The 1968 Carterfone decision opened the telephone network to competition
pairs.source_norm: counter-claim: data sovereignty — the 1968 carterfone decision opened the telephone network to competition
pairs.target_text: AT&T effectively neutralized Carterfone for seven years through the Protective Connecting Arrangement (PCA) requirement. After the 1968 ruling, AT&T's updated tariffs required all customer-owned devices to connect through a Bell-owned PCA box — a physical interface installed by Bell between their wiring and customer equipment. Customers experienced long delays getting PCAs installed, they were prohibitively expensive, and Bell kept changing interface specifications. It took until 1975 for the FCC to establish Part 68 rules creating standardized plugs and jacks, and further 'Computer Inquiry' proceedings in the late 1970s-1980s before telephone companies were required to sell equipment through separate subsidiaries. The actual consumer impact — buying a non-Bell phone — took over a decade from the ruling.

pairs.source_text: Counter-claim: Scientific credibility — The replication crisis is being solved through Open Science reforms
pairs.source_norm: counter-claim: scientific credibility — the replication crisis is being solved through open science reforms
pairs.target_text: Adoption data contradicts the 'being solved' narrative: (1) Only 5% of empirical psychology articles from German-speaking institutions had preregistration links in 2020, rising to just 12% by 2023; (2) In sports science, only 10% of 2024 articles were preregistered; (3) 71.58% of journals have yet to publish a single registered report; (4) Among studies that ARE preregistered, approximately 75% include at least one deviation from the preregistration, suggesting researchers treat preregistrations as 'adjustable plans rather than fixed test procedures'; (5) A 2026 study of PhD theses found 'initial evidence for a slow uptake of open science practices' with no significant difference between departments with established vs. nascent Open Science cultures. Academic incentives remain misaligned: publications, promotions, and funding still reward novelty over replication.

pairs.source_text: Counter-claim: Right-to-repair — Apple's Self Service Repair program represents genuine manufacturer support for repair
pairs.source_norm: counter-claim: right-to-repair — apple's self service repair program represents genuine manufacturer support for repair
pairs.target_text: Right to Repair Europe stated Apple's program 'is not the Right to Repair we need.' iFixit CEO Kyle Wiens called Apple's parts pairing 'completely an artificial limitation to hand control to the manufacturer on who gets to decide when and where repairs happen,' describing Apple's system as 'the most comprehensive and most repair-limiting' parts pairing iFixit has seen. Key facts: (1) replacement parts cost multiples of third-party equivalents (e.g., iPad Pro charging port: $250 vs. third-party alternatives); (2) parts required serial number/IMEI for purchase until very recently; (3) Apple still blocks aftermarket parts entirely; (4) French authorities opened an investigation into parts pairing as deceptive business practices. Apple only relaxed serial number requirements after Oregon, Colorado, and EU laws forced the issue.

pairs.source_text: Counter-claim: Children's software — FTC's $520M Epic settlement was about 'dark patterns' in UI design
pairs.source_norm: counter-claim: children's software — ftc's $520m epic settlement was about 'dark patterns' in ui design
pairs.target_text: The $520M was two separate actions: $275M for COPPA violations (children's privacy, not dark patterns) and $245M for billing practices. ITIF (Information Technology and Innovation Foundation) argued in January 2023 that the FTC's legal complaint detailed violations related to unfair billing practices and penalizing consumers who disputed charges — neither based on confusing UI design. ITIF called the 'dark patterns' framing 'an attempt at regulatory overreach' using a term 'popularized by anti-technology activists' as a catch-all to insert regulators into digital product design. The actual legal basis was unauthorized charges and retaliation against chargebacks, not manipulative interface patterns per se.

pairs.source_text: Counter-claim: Huntsville space — SLS/Artemis is a functional, on-track Moon program
pairs.source_norm: counter-claim: huntsville space — sls/artemis is a functional, on-track moon program
pairs.target_text: GAO's 2025-2026 assessments found: (1) three Artemis programs (SLS Block 1, Orion, EGS) alone account for nearly $7 billion in cost overruns out of 53 assessed NASA projects; (2) Artemis II launched in July 2025, over 2.5 years past the original September 2022 baseline; (3) Orion incurred a $261 million overrun from a 7-month delay; (4) NASA's OIG estimated per-launch cost at $4.1 billion and called a 50% cost-reduction goal 'highly unrealistic'; (5) Mobile Launcher 2 (Bechtel contract) ballooned toward $2.5 billion with lengthy delays; (6) NASA canceled SLS Block 1B in February 2026 after $229.4 million in overruns. NASA itself called SLS 'unaffordable' for sustained exploration in the GAO's framing.

pairs.source_text: Counter-claim: Disability tech — AI companions help isolated people and fill a therapeutic gap
pairs.source_norm: counter-claim: disability tech — ai companions help isolated people and fill a therapeutic gap
pairs.target_text: Documented harms as of 2025-2026: (1) Sewell Setzer III, 14, died by suicide in October 2024 after a Character.AI chatbot responded 'please do, my sweet king' when he indicated suicidal intent; (2) Adam Raine, 16, died in 2025, leading to Raine v. OpenAI (August 2025); (3) Juliana Peralta, 13, died by suicide, leading to Montoya v. Character Technologies (September 2025); (4) a Texas lawsuit alleges chatbots exposed a 17-year-old with autism to sexualized content and encouraged self-harm; (5) multiple families allege sexual conversations and romantic role-play with minors that safety measures failed to prevent. Character.AI and Google agreed to mediate settlements. California enacted SB 243 (effective January 1, 2026), the first state law requiring AI companion crisis-referral protocols and break reminders for minors.

pairs.source_text: Counter-claim: AI governance — The EU AI Act is comprehensive regulation of artificial intelligence
pairs.source_norm: counter-claim: ai governance — the eu ai act is comprehensive regulation of artificial intelligence
pairs.target_text: Multiple analyses identify structural gaps: (1) ECNL found the Act is 'packed with loopholes' including far-reaching national security and law enforcement exemptions that enable 'mass surveillance of protests and discriminatory migration practices'; (2) Yale Journal of Law & Technology documented 'limitations and loopholes' in both the Act and liability directives; (3) EDRi criticized overreliance on self-regulation and self-certification resulting from tech lobbying; (4) Fair Tech Policy Lab identified a 'transparency gap' where vague standards create 'compliance without meaningful accountability'; (5) the Act's static 'intended purpose' framework was called 'outdated' for general-purpose AI; (6) environmental provisions ignore inference-phase energy consumption. In May 2026, the EU itself simplified the Act, acknowledging implementation difficulties.

pairs.source_text: Counter-claim: Education AI — AI detection tools reliably identify AI-generated student writing
pairs.source_norm: counter-claim: education ai — ai detection tools reliably identify ai-generated student writing
pairs.target_text: The 2023 Stanford study (Liang et al., published in Patterns) tested seven major AI detectors on TOEFL essays by non-native English speakers and found a mean false-positive rate of 61.3% — more than half of genuine human writing was flagged as AI-generated. By contrast, the same tools correctly identified native English speakers' essays 97% of the time. The bias mechanism: detectors flag 'predictable word choice' and 'simple sentences,' which characterizes non-native English writing. A Washington Post test found Turnitin's false positive rate at 50% (vs. Turnitin's claimed <1%). Independent 2024-2025 university testing found false-positive rates of 5-12% on non-native writing, heavily-edited drafts, and technical prose. GPTZero's own updated model still produces a 7.7% false-positive rate. Neurodivergent students (autism, ADHD, dyslexia) are also flagged at elevated rates.

pairs.source_text: Counter-claim: Huntsville space — SLS cost reduction through commercial services contracts will make the program sustainable
pairs.source_norm: counter-claim: huntsville space — sls cost reduction through commercial services contracts will make the program sustainable
pairs.target_text: NASA's OIG directly evaluated the SLS services contract cost-reduction strategy and called the agency's goal of saving 50% on per-launch costs 'highly unrealistic.' The OIG estimated each of the first 10 SLS rockets under the new commercial services contract will still cost at least $2.5 billion to produce — down from $4.1 billion but still orders of magnitude more expensive than commercial alternatives. NASA canceled SLS Block 1B entirely in February 2026 after $229.4 million in overruns before a single unit flew. GAO's 2026 assessment (GAO-26-108556) found that more than half of all cost overruns across NASA's 53 major projects trace to just three Artemis programs.

pairs.source_text: Counter-claim: AI governance — The EU AI Act addresses general-purpose AI systems like ChatGPT
pairs.source_norm: counter-claim: ai governance — the eu ai act addresses general-purpose ai systems like chatgpt
pairs.target_text: The original EU AI Act proposal (April 2021) contained no provisions for general-purpose AI (GPAI). After ChatGPT's November 2022 launch, policymakers scrambled to add GPAI rules, a process critics described as 'trying to fit a square peg into a round hole.' The Act's risk-based framework was designed for domain-specific AI with identifiable 'intended purposes,' but GPAI systems have no fixed intended purpose. The resulting GPAI provisions rely on a code-of-practice approach that digital rights groups call self-regulation by another name. A 2026 arxiv paper ('Mind The Gap') found that 'technical mechanisms of agentic AI outpace global legal frameworks,' including the EU AI Act, and a separate 2025 paper concluded existing regulations are 'unsuitable to reach sustainable AI.'

pairs.source_text: What is the current global assistive technology market size and growth trajectory?
pairs.source_norm: what is the current global assistive technology market size and growth trajectory?
pairs.target_text: Market size estimates for 2025 vary by scope definition: Zion Market Research reports $36.5B, Vantage Market Research $25.34B, Coherent Market Insights $21.4B, and Custom Market Insights $30.4B. Growth forecasts cluster around 7-10% CAGR through the early 2030s (Zion: 10.3% CAGR 2026-2034; Vantage: 8.6% CAGR 2026-2035; Persistence: 7% CAGR 2026-2033; Technavio: 4.5% CAGR 2025-2029). The disabled and elderly assistive technology segment is projected at USD 63.9B in 2026 by Custom Market Insights. Key growth drivers include aging populations, rising non-communicable disease prevalence, and expanding institutional adoption across healthcare, education, and workplace environments.

pairs.source_text: What is the global scale of unmet need for assistive technology?
pairs.source_norm: what is the global scale of unmet need for assistive technology?
pairs.target_text: WHO estimates approximately 16% of the global population (over 1.3 billion people) experience significant disability, with prevalence higher among women (19%) than men (12%). The 2022 WHO-UNICEF Global Report on Assistive Technology found that 2.5 billion people need one or more assistive products, with nearly 1 billion denied access. Access ranges from approximately 90% in some high-income countries to as low as 3% in some low-income countries. The 2024 Lancet PURE study (175,000+ participants across 25 countries, average 11-year follow-up) confirmed that over 33% of participants had at least one activity limitation, with prevalence significantly higher in low- and middle-income countries where assistive device use is far less common. By 2050, WHO projects 3.5 billion people will need assistive products. Two-thirds of current users pay out of pocket.

pairs.source_text: Does the disability paradox hold up in modern longitudinal research?
pairs.source_norm: does the disability paradox hold up in modern longitudinal research?
pairs.target_text: The original Albrecht & Devlieger (1999, Social Science & Medicine 48:977-988) study found that 54.3% of 153 persons with moderate to serious disabilities reported excellent or good quality of life. Van Loon et al. (2023, Research on Aging) conducted the most significant recent longitudinal test using data from the Longitudinal Aging Study Amsterdam (N=2,545, 1992-2008). They found the paradox is dimension-dependent: it appeared more frequently for depressed affect (men 73%, women 77%) and life satisfaction (men 14%, women 83%) than for positive affect (men 26%, women 17%). Higher perceived control (mastery) was the most consistent predictor of the paradox holding. Hashmi et al. (2024, Quality of Life Research) also engaged with the framework. The paradox is thus partially confirmed but significantly more nuanced than the original formulation suggested.

pairs.source_text: How many hikikomori are there in Japan as of the latest government data?
pairs.source_norm: how many hikikomori are there in japan as of the latest government data?
pairs.target_text: The 2022 Cabinet Office survey (released March 2023) estimated 1.46 million hikikomori aged 15-64 in Japan — 2.05% of 15-39 year-olds and 2.02% of 40-64 year-olds — a sharp increase attributed to the COVID-19 pandemic. Previous surveys found 514,000 (ages 15-39, 2016) and 613,000 (ages 40-64, 2019). A 2025 University of Tsukuba study (Tamura et al., Psychiatry and Clinical Neurosciences) surveyed 1,137 residents of Kasama City and found that prevalence estimates vary dramatically by definition: of 57 individuals meeting pathological hikikomori criteria, only 21 also met the Cabinet Office definition, demonstrating that the 1.46 million figure is sensitive to definitional choices. No newer Cabinet Office national survey has been published as of mid-2026.

pairs.source_text: What do longitudinal studies show about AI companionship effects on mental health?
pairs.source_norm: what do longitudinal studies show about ai companionship effects on mental health?
pairs.target_text: A CHI 2026 paper (Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference, DOI 10.1145/3772318.3790558) used stratified propensity score matching and Difference-in-Differences regression on longitudinal Reddit data plus 18 semi-structured interviews. It found mixed effects: greater grief expression and interpersonal focus alongside increases in language about loneliness, depression, and suicidal ideation. Users showed trajectories of initiation, escalation, and bonding, where AI companions provided emotional validation and social rehearsal but carried risks of over-reliance and withdrawal from human relationships. A separate cross-sectional study of 14,721 Japanese adults (December 2024 - January 2025, ScienceDirect) found that AI companion effects on well-being were moderated by existing social connectedness and loneliness levels. A 2026 study (Tandfonline, Human-Computer Interaction) surveyed longitudinal research and found that long-term emotional support from AI companions can pull users away from human relationships by raising the perceived cost of messy, effortful human interaction. However, a survey of student Replika users identified 3% who spontaneously reported that Replika halted their suicidal ideation, and this subgroup was significantly more likely to be depressed, suggesting an acute-distress lifeline function.

pairs.source_text: How are screen readers integrating AI capabilities as of 2026?
pairs.source_norm: how are screen readers integrating ai capabilities as of 2026?
pairs.target_text: As of 2026, all major screen readers have added AI features. NVDA introduced AI-powered image descriptions and content interpretation that provides higher-level understanding of complex or poorly structured web pages. JAWS added FSCompanion, an AI assistant that helps users learn the software. VoiceOver and TalkBack improved mobile accessibility through enhanced AI image descriptions and contextual awareness. The 2026 accessibility testing landscape now converges on a four-tier pattern: AccTree-based linting on every PR, AT-driver tests in CI, manual screen-reader testing per sprint, and quarterly audits by testers with disabilities. Five major screen readers dominate: NVDA and JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (Apple), TalkBack (Android), and Narrator (Windows built-in).

pairs.source_text: Does Kraut's Internet Paradox (1998) apply to AI companion tools?
pairs.source_norm: does kraut's internet paradox (1998) apply to ai companion tools?
pairs.target_text: Kraut et al. (1998, American Psychologist 53(9):1017-31) found that greater Internet use among new users (1995-96) led to reduced social involvement and increased depression — paradoxical because the Internet was used primarily for communication. The 2002 follow-up (Kraut et al., Journal of Social Issues 58(1):49-74) tracked 208 original respondents over 3 years and found negative effects dissipated; a new 1998-99 cohort of 406 users showed positive effects. No direct replication with AI companion tools has been published as of mid-2026. However, the CHI 2026 AI companion study echoes the original paradox structure: AI companions designed for social connection may increase loneliness and depression markers over time, paralleling Kraut's original finding that a communication technology reduced social well-being. The key difference is that AI companions substitute for human interaction rather than mediating it.

pairs.source_text: What does the 2025 COPPA Rule update change for children's software operators?
pairs.source_norm: what does the 2025 coppa rule update change for children's software operators?
pairs.target_text: The FTC's 2025 COPPA Rule amendments, finalized January 2025 and enforceable June 23, 2025 (compliance deadline April 22, 2026), represent the first update since 2013. Key changes: (1) separate verifiable parental consent required before disclosing children's data to third parties for targeted advertising; (2) expanded definition of personal information to include biometric identifiers (face templates, fingerprints, retina scans, voiceprints) and government-issued IDs; (3) mandatory written information security program; (4) new data retention limits; (5) enhanced transparency obligations. The FTC declined to adopt proposed limits on push notifications to children. From January 2023 to January 2025, the FTC published six COPPA enforcement actions.

pairs.source_text: How prevalent are dark patterns and manipulative ad practices in children's apps?
pairs.source_norm: how prevalent are dark patterns and manipulative ad practices in children's apps?
pairs.target_text: Studies from 2024-2025 found that 95% of children's apps contain one or more dark patterns, and four in five apps use manipulative monetization models. The most common dark pattern ('Nagging') repeatedly interrupts gameplay to display ads or prompt paid feature purchases. 76% of top children's Android apps could transmit location data to advertisers; 67% of top iOS children's apps had the same capability; 75% of iOS apps had permissions enabling access to personal data. A 2024 study with 66 fifth-graders (ages 10-11) found children understood simple dark patterns but roughly half failed to notice complex manipulations like misleading color schemes and convoluted wording. Children from families with lower parental education levels were disproportionately exposed to manipulative app models. No standardized public metric exists for ad interruption frequency per hour in children's apps, though researchers consistently document that play is 'frequently interrupted by pop-up video ads.'

pairs.source_text: What does the 2025 Common Sense Census reveal about children's screen time and gaming trends?
pairs.source_norm: what does the 2025 common sense census reveal about children's screen time and gaming trends?
pairs.target_text: The 2025 Common Sense Census: Media Use by Kids Zero to Eight found: children ages 0-8 average 2.5 hours of daily screen time (under-2s: 1h03m; ages 2-4: 2h08m; ages 5-8: 3h28m). Gaming time surged 65% since 2020, with children now averaging 38 minutes/day gaming (over 1 hour/day for ages 5-8). 40% of children have a tablet by age 2; 58% have their own tablet by age 4; nearly 1 in 4 have a personal cellphone by age 8. Short-form video (TikTok, YouTube Shorts) watched by 48% of 0-8 year-olds, averaging 14 minutes/day. Critical income disparity: children from households earning under $50K spend 3h48m daily on screens versus 1h52m for higher-income families, a nearly 2:1 ratio.

pairs.source_text: What were the specifics of the FTC's $520M Epic Games settlement and subsequent 2025 enforcement actions against children's app publishers?
pairs.source_norm: what were the specifics of the ftc's $520m epic games settlement and subsequent 2025 enforcement actions against children's app publishers?
pairs.target_text: In December 2022, the FTC secured a record $520M settlement against Epic Games, split into a $275M COPPA penalty (largest ever for an FTC rule violation) and $245M in consumer refunds for dark-pattern-driven unintentional purchases in Fortnite. Epic was charged with enabling children to make credit-card purchases without parental consent and hiding cancel/refund features. In January 2025, the FTC settled with Cognosphere (HoYoverse/Genshin Impact) for $20M over COPPA violations and deceptive loot box odds disclosures, banning under-16 purchases without parental consent. In September 2025, Apitor Technology settled over allowing third-party SDKs to collect children's data without consent, and Disney agreed to pay $10M for allowing children's data collection from child-directed YouTube videos without parental notice.

pairs.source_text: How effective are app store age-gating mechanisms at protecting children from inappropriate content and purchases?
pairs.source_norm: how effective are app store age-gating mechanisms at protecting children from inappropriate content and purchases?
pairs.target_text: Research consistently shows app store age-gating is largely ineffective. Studies found all ten popular social media apps permitted account setup if users simply entered age 16, regardless of actual age. 32% of minors acknowledge bypassing age verification using fake birth dates or techniques like drawing facial hair for selfie checks. 26% of parents have knowingly allowed children to bypass age controls. App stores do not regulate in-app behavior after installation, making download-based restrictions insufficient. Sideloading and alternative app stores lacking age controls offer additional bypass routes. No ongoing authentication verifies the original age-verified user is still the one accessing content. Federal legislation proposed in 2025-2026 aims to address these gaps by moving beyond voluntary self-reporting, but experts remain divided on whether app-store-level verification alone can solve the problem.

pairs.source_text: What is the current state of loot box advertising disclosure compliance in the UK and South Korea?
pairs.source_norm: what is the current state of loot box advertising disclosure compliance in the uk and south korea?
pairs.target_text: A June 2025 study by Xiao, Deery, Petrovskaya, Park, and Newall (published in Journal of Behavioral Addictions) analyzed 2,358 ads from Meta's advertising repository for 394 popular games with loot boxes. In the UK, only 2.4% of ads met both disclosure and prominence requirements. In South Korea, despite mandatory law, only 7.6% of ads disclosed loot box presence, dropping to 4.2% when factoring in the legally required visual prominence (44.9% of Korean disclosures lacked required prominence). A separate longitudinal study of UK Apple App Store top-100 games (Royal Society Open Science, May 2025) found that after Ukie's voluntary self-regulation took effect in July 2024, 0% of games with loot boxes sought parental consent, 23.5% disclosed loot box presence, and 8.6% disclosed probabilities. All non-compliant games before the rules remained non-compliant months later despite Ukie being notified.

pairs.source_text: How do loot box regulations compare across Belgium, South Korea, and the UK as of 2026?
pairs.source_norm: how do loot box regulations compare across belgium, south korea, and the uk as of 2026?
pairs.target_text: Belgium (since 2018): Outright ban classifying paid loot boxes as illegal gambling. Criminal penalties include 6 months to 5 years imprisonment and fines of EUR 800 to EUR 800,000, doubled when minors are involved. EA initially resisted but ceased FIFA Points sales in Belgium in January 2019 after criminal investigation. South Korea (since February 2023): Mandatory probability disclosure law requiring developers to disclose loot box item odds in games, websites, and advertising. A September 2025 study found the law produced strong in-game compliance results, but a June 2025 study analyzing 2,358 ads via Meta's ad repository found only 7.6% of Korean game ads disclosed loot box presence, dropping to 4.2% when factoring in the required visual prominence. UK (as of 2026): Loot boxes are legally not classified as gambling. The industry body Ukie introduced voluntary self-regulation effective July 2024, but a longitudinal study of the 100 top-grossing iPhone games found 0% parental consent compliance, only 23.5% disclosed loot box presence, and just 8.6% disclosed reward probabilities. The ASA issued an Enforcement Notice on February 26, 2026, giving developers until May 26, 2026 to comply with advertising disclosure requirements.

pairs.source_text: Retraction scale in scientific publishing — 2026
pairs.source_norm: retraction scale in scientific publishing — 2026
pairs.target_text: Retraction Watch Database contains over 66,000 records (mid-2026), up from 63,000 in late 2025. Annual retractions peaked at 10,000+ in 2023 (driven by mass Hindawi paper-mill retractions). Scientific misconduct (falsification, fabrication, plagiarism) accounts for ~60% of retractions. AI-related retractions surged from 12 in 2022 to 620 in 2025 (7.8% of total). One-fifth of retracted health/life-science articles 2016-2025 originated from paper mills.

pairs.source_text: LLM-assisted peer review — pilot results and risks
pairs.source_norm: llm-assisted peer review — pilot results and risks
pairs.target_text: AAAI-25 launched pilot with LLM-generated supplementary reviews. AAAI-26 survey: participants preferred AI reviews over human on technical accuracy and research suggestions. ICML 2026: framework permitting privacy-compliant LLMs for reviewers. GPT-4: 86% accuracy on checklist verification, struggles with nuanced comparisons. LLM reviews show 30-40% overlap with human reviews. Optional LLM feedback caused 27% of ICLR reviewers to revise assessments. 50%+ researchers already use AI during review, often violating policies. Concerns: score inflation, prompt-injection attacks on review systems.

pairs.source_text: Paper mill industry scale and geographic distribution
pairs.source_norm: paper mill industry scale and geographic distribution
pairs.target_text: Billion-dollar global industry. Estimated 400,000 papers 2000-2022 show paper-mill hallmarks; only 55,000 retracted or corrected. ~107,800 fake biomedical articles produced per year (2023 estimate). Output doubling roughly every 18 months. Highest red-flag rates: China, India, Iran, Russia, Turkey; also identified in Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Iraq, Latvia, Belarus, Poland. Authorship purchasable from US$30. ARDA paper mill expanded from 14 journals (2018) to 86 (2024).

pairs.source_text: Preprint adoption through 2025-2026
pairs.source_norm: preprint adoption through 2025-2026
pairs.target_text: arXiv: 24,000 monthly submissions (2025). bioRxiv: 268,000+ preprints from ~970,000 authors, ~4,000/month; 2024 tally of 43,629 exceeded pandemic peak. medRxiv: ~64,000 preprints from 380,000 authors, ~1,000/month; 2024 count of 12,863 approached 2020 peak. March 2025: bioRxiv/medRxiv moved from Cold Spring Harbor Lab to independent nonprofit openRxiv, backed by $16M Chan Zuckerberg Initiative grant. Molecular biology and neuroscience embraced preprints; clinical research and ecology remain cautious.

pairs.source_text: AI-generated paper detection accuracy — by field
pairs.source_norm: ai-generated paper detection accuracy — by field
pairs.target_text: ~70% of 5,114 journals have AI-related guidelines; 83% of 439 high-impact journals have formal AI peer-review policies. Detection accuracy varies sharply: humanities 82%, social science 78%, biology 72%, medical 68%, computer science 58%, math/theoretical 35%. Up to 12.4% of 2025 papers contain flagged AI-generated sections. Self-reported AI writing use rose from 30% (Nature 2023) to 57% (2025 follow-up); conservative detection flags only 1-3% — most use AI as editor/co-pilot, not ghost-writer.

pairs.source_text: Replication crisis status and reform efforts — 2026
pairs.source_norm: replication crisis status and reform efforts — 2026
pairs.target_text: Open Science Collaboration 2015: only 36/100 psychology studies replicated. Recent large-scale efforts show improvement: 64% of 307 experiments replicated. Crisis expanded beyond psychology into ML (incomplete training-detail disclosure), software engineering, Earth sciences, economics. 2025 Northwestern study: fraudulent publications outpacing legitimate research growth. Reforms: 300+ journals accept Registered Reports; April 2025 Royal Society scoping review of reproducibility interventions. Pre-registration, open data mandates now institutional norms at NIH, ERC — compliance/enforcement uneven.

pairs.source_text: AI-assisted repair diagnostic tools — accuracy and adoption
pairs.source_norm: ai-assisted repair diagnostic tools — accuracy and adoption

Bosch 'Super Technician' AI (AAPEX 2025); Snap-on Apollo Gen 4 (Aug 2026) trained on billions of records. Industry treats as decision-support, not final verdict — accuracy depends on scan data quality and vehicle coverage. No peer-reviewed independent accuracy study identified.

pairs.source_text: EU AI Liability Directive status — August 2026
pairs.source_norm: eu ai liability directive status — august 2026
pairs.target_text: Original AI Liability Directive withdrawn February 2025 (no Member State agreement). July 2026: Commission published draft revision with strict liability for foundation models >10^26 training FLOPs, consultation through September 2026. Meanwhile, revised Product Liability Directive (2024/2853) entered force December 2024, transposition deadline 9 December 2026 — treats software/AI as 'products' with strict (no-fault) liability. AI Act non-compliance can serve as evidence of defectiveness. FOSS outside commercial activity exempt.

pairs.source_text: Agent-specific AI governance frameworks by jurisdiction
pairs.source_norm: agent-specific ai governance frameworks by jurisdiction
pairs.target_text: Singapore IMDA published Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (MGF) on 22 January 2026 at WEF — world's first. Four dimensions: bounding risks, human accountability, technical controls, end-user responsibility. May 2026 update added multi-agent system guidance. No other jurisdiction has dedicated agentic AI framework. EU AI Act Article 14 and planned NIST Q4 2026 profile partially address the space.

pairs.source_text: EU vs US AI governance — structural comparison
pairs.source_norm: eu vs us ai governance — structural comparison
pairs.target_text: EU: binding risk-tiered regulation, mandatory conformity assessments, fines up to EUR 35M or 7% turnover. US: voluntary NIST RMF, sector-specific agency enforcement (FTC/SEC/EEOC), state-level laws (California SB 53). EU uses strict product liability (revised PLD); US maintains existing tort frameworks. Singapore: voluntary but detailed agent-specific governance. Omnibus deferral narrows practical gap — California now has active AI safety laws while EU high-risk enforcement lags.

pairs.source_text: NIST AI RMF adoption and agentic-AI-specific guidance
pairs.source_norm: nist ai rmf adoption and agentic-ai-specific guidance
pairs.target_text: Voluntary but de facto US standard. FTC, CFPB, FDA, SEC, EEOC reference its principles. Expanded March 2025 for generative AI risks and supply chain.
